title: Approving a line moves its Quoted inventory part to In stock
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • Signed in as an Owner or Admin, at one location {Location} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • {Part}: an inventory part at {Location} with stock on hand, used only by this case (for example part number ZZAUTOTEST-SV4802-01 with 5 in stock).
  • {Work order}: a work order for a customer used only by this case (for example "ZZAUTOTEST SV4802 Approve Line"), open on its Lines tab.
  • {Line}: a line on {Work order} showing "Needs Approval", with its Approve and Decline buttons.
  • {Part} requested on {Line} from Inventory, quantity 1, showing "Quoted".
custom_steps:
1. On {Work order}, click Approve on {Line}. Do not refresh the page.
  2. Refresh the page.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Line} shows Approved.
  • Step 1: without any page refresh, {Part} changes from "Quoted" to "In stock", and its "Pick" action is shown.
  • Step 2: after the refresh, {Part} still shows "In stock" with the "Pick" action.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Jira SV-4802 "Inventory Part Remains in Quoted Status after Line Status Changes from Need Approval to Approved" (Bug, Done, fix version v0.43 released 11 Nov 2025; epic SV-4796 "V0.43 - Regression Testing Bugs"): Expected Result and Steps to Reproduce; developer comment (Dusan Bulovan, 5 Nov 2025) that a page refresh showed the correct status, so the fix is on screen; fix verified on staging 7 Nov 2025 (Edit Line window and bulk edit) and on production 12 Nov 2025 (Nebojsa Glavinic). Read 8 Oct 2026. Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • SV-4802 Expected Result: “The inventory part status should automatically update from `Quoted` to `In stock` with action `Pick`”
  • SV-4802 Steps to Reproduce, step 3: “Change the line status to `Approved`/`Authorized`”
  • SV-4802 comment, Dusan Bulovan, 5 Nov 2025: “Also, page refresh gives the correct part status, which is usually an indicator of FE issue.”
